paragraphs.text: Last September, our school started a Reading Club to help students enjoy books. It meets every Tuesday afternoon in the school library for about an hour. Members choose a book together, read it at home, and then meet to share their ideas.

At first, only eight students joined. The club adviser, Miss Yang, invited some senior students to recommend their favourite books at the school gate. Soon more students became interested, and now the club has over forty members. 'I used to think reading was boring,' says Lin Tao, a club member. 'But when I talk about a story with others, I find more fun in it.' This term, the club plans to invite a local writer to talk about how stories are created.
